headline: US-Iran war costs spiral past $37bn as oil spikes, RBA rate hike risk rises — GOOG and MSFT earnings due tonight US time.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: GOOG dipped last night as investors got nervous ahead of tonight's Q2 earnings (US time). The delay of Google's flagship Gemini 3.5 Pro model has rattled some confidence, with Chinese AI rivals closing the gap. Markets are pricing in uncertainty about how much Google is spending on AI versus what it's earning back.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft slipped last night ahead of its own Q4 2026 earnings report (also due tonight US time). Investors are cautious about whether the company's heavy AI investment is translating into revenue growth. Morningstar rates the stock fairly valued at current levels.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two eased last night in line with the broader NASDAQ softness. There's no major negative news — GTA V continues to sell steadily and GTA 6 anticipation remains high. The dip looks like general market caution rather than anything company-specific.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up today, likely benefiting from Google's new Gemini Flash model releases and the broader AI news cycle. Still well below your cost base at -15.9% overall, but today's session was a small positive.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS ticked up slightly today. There's some emerging positive news — a new report shows lithium demand is again outpacing supply globally, with $15 billion in investment forecast to 2035. That's a longer-term tailwind, but short-term lithium prices remain under pressure and PLS is still 38% below your entry price.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS edged up today, tracking last night's solid S&P 500 and NASDAQ gains. The broad US market had a good session last night, lifting this ETF which holds essentially the entire US sharemarket.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG had a quiet positive session today, up 0.41% as the ASX 200 gained ground. This diversified fund spreads across global shares and bonds, so it tends to move steadily — exactly as intended.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE slipped today, likely weighed down by Middle East tensions and the ongoing US-Iran conflict adding risk to emerging market sentiment. Geopolitical stress tends to push investors away from riskier emerging markets and into safer assets.

watch_today.title: GOOG & MSFT Earnings Tonight (US Time) — Big Night
watch_today.detail: Both Alphabet (GOOG) and Microsoft (MSFT) report Q2/Q4 earnings tonight when US markets open (~11:30pm AEST). This is the biggest event for your portfolio this week. Expect significant price moves — up or down — by tomorrow morning. For a long-term holder, don't panic at a single-night swing in either direction.

watch_today.title: MSFT Earnings: Hold Steady Through the Noise
watch_today.detail: Microsoft is reporting tonight. The stock is down 10% from your buy-in price overall, but the long-term AI and cloud story remains solid. One earnings result won't change that thesis. Sit tight and see what the numbers say — Morningstar currently rates it fairly valued.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Small Green Shoot, But Still Deep in the Red
watch_today.detail: Pilbara ticked up 0.73% today and new data shows global lithium demand is outpacing supply again — a long-term positive for PLS. But the stock is still 38% below your entry price and short-term lithium prices remain depressed. No reason to sell; the long-term case is intact, but patience is required.

watch_today.title: Oil Spiking on Iran War — Watch Inflation Impact
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) jumped 2.2% last night to $86.77/barrel as the US-Iran conflict escalates and Houthi forces are turning oil tankers around. Higher oil means higher fuel and goods prices in Australia, which increases the chance the RBA hikes interest rates rather than cuts. This is worth watching closely over the coming weeks.

watch_today.title: RBA Rate Hike Risk Rising — Mortgage Holders Take Note
watch_today.detail: Multiple analysts are now saying the RBA is twice as likely to raise interest rates as they were before the Iran conflict drove up oil and fuel prices. This affects mortgage repayments directly. If you have a variable rate mortgage, it's worth checking your buffer.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — Recovering Slowly, AI Newsflow Supportive
watch_today.detail: Your Global X AI ETF is still 15.9% below cost, but today's 0.76% gain and a burst of positive AI news (new Google Gemini models, Chinese AI competition heating up) keeps the long-term story intact. This is a hold — the AI theme is far from over.

world.summary: The US-Iran conflict is escalating sharply, with costs now topping $37.5 billion, oil spiking and Houthi forces disrupting global shipping. A massive airport fire in Bordeaux killed firefighters and grounded flights. Europe is caught between China trade tensions and its own economic interests. And Australian travel warnings for the Middle East have been upgraded.

stories.title: US Renews Iran Strikes, Trump Threatens to Hit Nuclear Site 'Very Heavily'
stories.why_it_matters: The US has resumed airstrikes on Iran, and President Trump is now openly threatening to hit 'Pickaxe Mountain' — believed to be a key Iranian nuclear facility — 'very heavily'. Defence Secretary Hegseth has put the total cost of the Iran war at $37.5 billion and rising. Houthi forces (Iran-backed fighters in Yemen) are forcing oil tankers to turn around in the Red Sea, disrupting global shipping lanes. For everyday Australians, this means higher fuel prices and potential supply chain disruptions — and a greater chance the RBA hikes interest rates as inflation rises.

stories.title: Australia Issues New Travel Warning for Middle East Countries
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian government has upgraded travel advice for several Middle East countries in response to the escalating US-Iran conflict. Australians are being urged to reconsider or avoid travel to affected regions. If you or family members have trips planned to the Middle East, check the latest DFAT advice immediately — the situation is fluid and conditions can deteriorate quickly.

stories.title: Huge Fire at Bordeaux Airport — Firefighters Killed, Flights Cancelled
stories.why_it_matters: A massive fire broke out at Bordeaux Airport in France, killing at least some firefighters and forcing the cancellation of all flights in and out of the airport. The blaze caused chaos for travellers across Europe. The cause is under investigation. If you have connections through Bordeaux or know anyone travelling via southern France, delays and diversions are likely to continue as the airport deals with the aftermath.

stories.title: Trump Pushes China Election Threat, But Files Show Russia's Heavy Hand
stories.why_it_matters: President Trump is publicly blaming China for interfering in US elections, but newly released documents apparently show it's Russia with the more significant and organised operation. This matters because it shapes US foreign policy — if Trump is focused on China as the threat while Russia operates more freely, it affects alliances, trade deals, and global stability in ways that ripple through to Australian export markets and security arrangements.

stories.title: Europe's China Dilemma: Free Trade vs Geopolitical Reality
stories.why_it_matters: Europe is caught in an uncomfortable position — it wants to maintain free trade with China for economic reasons, but US pressure and security concerns are pushing it to decouple. The EU is weighing tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles and tech goods while trying not to trigger a trade war that would hurt European manufacturers. For Australia, which also trades heavily with China, how Europe navigates this tension will shape the global trade environment we all operate in.

markets.summary: Last night the US had a solid session — NASDAQ up 1.3% and S&P 500 up 0.9% — but your US holdings (GOOG, MSFT, TTWO) all dipped slightly on earnings caution. The ASX closed up 0.34% today at 8,823. Oil jumped hard (+2.2%) on Iran tensions, and gold hit a new high above $4,124/oz. The Aussie dollar is basically flat at 70 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Solid session today — up 0.34% to close at 8,823.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Good night last night — up 0.89% to 7,509.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Tech-heavy NASDAQ had a strong night, up 1.29% to 25,837.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil jumped 2.2% to $86.77/barrel as the US-Iran war escalates and Houthi forces disrupt Red Sea shipping.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold surged 1.3% to a new high of $4,124/oz — investors piling into safe-haven assets amid geopolitical stress.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar is essentially flat at 70.05 US cents.

politics.summary: The RBA is under intense scrutiny today, with analysts warning a rate hike is now twice as likely as it was before the Iran war drove oil prices higher. Inflation is overtaking housing as Australians' biggest economic worry. And a new RBA study finds most Aussies don't actually understand how interest rates work.

stories.title: RBA Rate Hike Now Twice as Likely as Iran War Pushes Fuel Prices Higher
stories.why_it_matters: Economists are now saying the probability of the RBA raising interest rates has doubled, driven by oil prices surging on the back of the US-Iran conflict. Higher oil means higher petrol, higher transport costs, and higher inflation across the board. If the RBA does hike, variable rate mortgage holders will see repayments increase again — the exact opposite of what most Australians have been hoping for.

stories.title: Inflation Now Aussies' Biggest Worry — Overtakes Housing
stories.why_it_matters: A new survey shows inflation has overtaken housing affordability as the number-one financial concern for everyday Australians. With oil prices jumping and global supply chains under stress from the Middle East conflict, cost-of-living pressures look set to worsen before they improve. This is the backdrop the RBA is navigating when it considers its next rate decision.

stories.title: Most Australians Don't Understand How Interest Rates Actually Work — RBA
stories.why_it_matters: A new RBA-commissioned study has found the majority of Australians don't have a clear understanding of how interest rate decisions flow through to their mortgage repayments, savings, or the broader economy. The RBA says this makes it harder for rate changes to have the intended effect, since people don't change spending behaviour in the expected ways. It's a surprising finding that raises questions about how the central bank communicates its decisions.

stories.title: 'Do Not Rule Out' a Rate Hike — Warning for Mortgage Holders
stories.why_it_matters: Leading economists are warning mortgage holders not to assume rates will only go down from here. The phrase 'do not rule out a rate hike' is appearing in analyst commentary for the first time in months, driven by the oil price surge from Middle East conflict. Anyone on a variable rate mortgage should be stress-testing their budget against a possible 0.25% increase.

ai.summary: Google launched three new lightweight Gemini models today while its flagship Gemini 3.5 Pro remains delayed — and Chinese AI models are closing the gap fast. Australia released an AI safety framework that researchers say lacks coherence. And new research warns that weak AI regulation may be worse than having no regulation at all.

stories.title: Google Launches Gemini 3.6 Flash and New Lite Models — But Flagship Still Delayed
stories.why_it_matters: Google today released three new AI models: Gemini 3.6 Flash (faster and cheaper), 3.5 Flash-Lite (for lightweight tasks), and 3.5 Flash Cyber (for security applications). These are smaller, quicker models designed to run more efficiently — think of them as the economy-class versions of Google's AI lineup. The big flagship model, Gemini 3.5 Pro, is still delayed, which has given Chinese rivals an opening to catch up. For Google shareholders, tonight's earnings will reveal how well the company is monetising all this AI investment.

stories.title: Chinese AI Model 'Kimi' Closing in on OpenAI and Anthropic as Google Slips
stories.why_it_matters: China's Kimi AI model — built by startup Moonshot AI — is now benchmarking close to OpenAI's GPT-4 and Anthropic's Claude on key performance tests, according to new data. This is significant because it shows the gap between US and Chinese AI is narrowing fast, despite US chip export restrictions designed to slow China down. For investors in AI-exposed stocks like GOOG or GXAI.AX, a more competitive global AI landscape means no single company can rest on its laurels.

stories.title: Australia's AI Safety Plan Released — But Is It Actually Coherent?
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian government has published its latest AI safety priorities, but researchers at The Conversation are already questioning whether the plan is internally consistent or practically enforceable. The framework covers things like algorithmic transparency and high-risk AI use cases, but critics say it lacks teeth and clear accountability mechanisms. With AI moving so fast, a vague regulatory plan may offer consumers false reassurance while letting harmful applications slip through the cracks.

stories.title: Researchers Warn: Weak AI Regulation Is Worse Than No Regulation
stories.why_it_matters: A new study from AI researchers argues that half-baked regulation — rules that sound good but are too vague to enforce — can actually make AI risks worse than having no rules at all. The reason: weak laws give companies legal cover to claim compliance while continuing risky practices, and give consumers false confidence. The researchers are calling for precise, enforceable standards rather than broad principles. This is directly relevant to the Australian framework released today.

sport.summary: NRL Round 21 kicks off Thursday night with Eels vs Panthers. There's judiciary drama with a Tigers player ban under scrutiny and a Souths star awaiting his fate. The new PNG Chiefs NRL team is building its roster for 2028, and the AFL's Giants are on track to miss the wildcard finals spot.

stories.title: NRL Judiciary: Tigers Ban Questioned, Souths Star Learns Fate
stories.why_it_matters: Fresh evidence has emerged challenging a Wests Tigers player's ban, described as 'bulls***' by some in the game — the case is being reviewed and could result in the suspension being overturned. Separately, a South Sydney Rabbitohs star appeared before the NRL judiciary today to learn his punishment for a charge from last weekend. With Souths hosting Storm on Friday night, the outcome directly affects their Round 21 lineup.

stories.title: Round 21 Tips and Expert Picks — Panthers the Team to Beat
stories.why_it_matters: Round 21 tips are out ahead of Thursday's opener between the Eels and Panthers at CommBank Stadium (7:50pm). Key matchups this week include Rabbitohs vs Storm (Friday), Cowboys vs Broncos (Saturday night in Townsville), and Bulldogs vs Warriors (Saturday). The Dolphins have a bye this round.

stories.title: PNG Chiefs NRL Team: Every Confirmed Signing So Far
stories.why_it_matters: The PNG Chiefs — set to join the NRL as the competition's 18th team — are actively building their roster and signing players ahead of their anticipated debut. CODE Sports is tracking every confirmed signing and the emerging best-17 picture. It's a historic expansion for the game and a big deal for Papua New Guinea, which has one of the most passionate rugby league fan bases in the world.

stories.title: AFL: Giants Set to Miss Finals Wildcard Spot, Top Six Locked In
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL ladder predictor has the GWS Giants on track to miss the wildcard finals spot, with the top six teams now effectively locked in for the rest of the home-and-away season. This means the Giants' season is on the line in their final rounds. The top six are fighting for positioning ahead of a finals series that's shaping up to be highly competitive.

stories.title: French Open Puts Rival Tennis Slams Under Pressure with €62m Prize Money Decision
stories.why_it_matters: The French Open has announced a massive €62 million (roughly AUD $103 million) prize pool, putting pressure on Wimbledon, the US Open and Australian Open to match it or risk losing prestige. The Roland Garros announcement sets a new benchmark for Grand Slam prize money globally. Players and agents will be watching how the other three majors respond ahead of their 2027 negotiations.
